title: Products of trivial fibrations are weak equivalences in a model category
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category [def-nagata-category] with a model structure: it has finite limits and colimits and classes $C,F,W$ of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences, $W$ is retract closed and satisfies two-out-of-three, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems. Here a weak factorization system $(A,B)$ means that every morphism factors as a map in $A$ followed by a map in $B$, and $A$ and $B$ are exactly the maps having, respectively, the left and right diagonal lifting properties against the other class. Let $J$ be a small set, possibly empty, and let $X_j,Y_j$ be objects whose products $\prod_{j\in J}X_j$ and $\prod_{j\in J}Y_j$ exist. If each $f_j:X_j\to Y_j$ is a trivial fibration, meaning that $f_j$ belongs to both $F$ and $W$, then the induced product map $\prod_j f_j:\prod_jX_j\to\prod_jY_j$ belongs to $W$.
